title.value: Adjusting Machine Learning Decisions for Equal Opportunity and Counterfactual Fairness
title.justification: The title of the paper clearly indicates the paper's focus.
title.quote: Adjusting Machine Learning Decisions for Equal Opportunity and Counterfactual Fairness

extractions.description: The paper develops algorithms that adjust existing ML decision-makers to produce algorithmic decisions that are both accurate and fair, without requiring refitting the ML method to data. It considers causal criteria for fairness, including equal counterfactual opportunity (eco) and counterfactual fairness (cf), and evaluates the algorithms on datasets about admissions, income, credit, and recidivism.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on fairness in machine learning decisions, which is related to Sustainable Development Goals, but is not central to the paper.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Machine learning (ml) methods have the potential to automate high-stakes decisions, such as bail admissions or credit lending, by analyzing and learning from historical data. But these algorithmic decisions may be unfair: in learning from historical data, they may replicate discriminatory practices from the past.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on fairness in machine learning decisions, and does not directly fall under any of the climate or ecologically-related sustainable development categories.
primary_category.quote: In this paper, we propose two algorithms that adjust fitted ML predictors to produce decisions that are fair. Our methods provide post-hoc adjustments to the predictors, without requiring that they be retrained.
